text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA
POLITIKA
- Inflation expectations drive up interest rates, street hard currency rates.
- Just 1.5 percent of all firms have so far been reorganized in keeping with new Law on Enterprises.
- Renowned U.S. business expert Isaac Adiges in Belgrade, to hold seminar.
- Interior ministry refuses to register independent pensioners' association.
NASA BORBA
- Bosnian presidency member Kresimir Zubak: We support restoration of ties, but not of former Yugoslavia.
- Opposition leader and Belgrade Mayor Zoran Djindjic says still too early to talk about co-leader Vuk Draskovic's candidacy for Serbian president.
- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic, under great pressure from Belgrade, unlikely to resign from post.
- Belgrade University students elect own parliament, first session on Monday.
- Bosnian Serbs, Yugoslavia strengthen economic ties, to introduce joint customs taxation by April 10.
- Kosovo Albanians' talks with Serbian authorities on education making little progress.
- Zastava Kragujevac automotive plant continues to search for foreign partner; March production just 150 cars instead of 2,500, as planned.
- Belgrade Mayor Zoran Djindjic announced major face-lift of city lasting one week.
- Kosovo Albanians launch new daily - Koha Ditore.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF
- Serbian opposition Democratic Party drafts platform for reorganization of Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serb Republic along lines of Great Britain and Northern Island.
- MONTENEGRO
POBJEDA
- Atrocious weather in Montenegro over past week-end.
- City of Herzeg Novi reconstructs local phone network.
- City of Savnik asks republic for more development funds.
- City of Pljevlja cites budget problems due to massive tax evasion.

- City of Foca, Bosnia, hopes to renew work on Buk Bijela hydroelectric power plant on river Drina funded together with Montenegro and worth $350 million. Foca hopes Bosnia reconstruction funds will help project. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 2224254
